questions.stemHtml: Identify the structure that does not form the laryngeal skeleton:
questions.solutionHtml:
A

A- Hyoid bone

B- Thyroid cartilage

C- Epiglottis

D- Arytenoid cartilage

  • Hyoid bone is not laryngeal cartilage.
  • Hyoid bone forms part of the hypopharyngeal framework.
  • Hypopharynx starts at the level of hyoid bone


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-717,718.

questions.stemHtml: Structure present behind the marked area is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Lesser wing of sphenoid
  • The marked area given in the question is Pterion

Pterion:

  • H shaped suture
  • Pterion is the name given to the region on the lateral aspect of the skull where four bones are joined
  • The pterion is a craniometric point near the sphenoid fontanelle of the skull. It is a point of convergence of the sutures between the frontal, parietal, temporal (the squamous part) & greater wing of sphenoid.
  • Deep to pterion, anterior branch of middle meningeal artery is present, on injury causes bleeding & a dangerous area in the skull.
  • In the given options the  Lesser wing of sphenoid is the  best answer.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-561.

questions.stem: In the lymphoid organs listed below, reticular fibers are not found in which organ?ThymusSpleenLymph nodeBone marrowSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1 only
  • The correct answer is Thymus
  • Thymic epithelial cells (also called epithelial-reticular cells or epitheliocytes), which make up the framework of the thymus. In the cortex as seen below, these cells are larger than the lymphocytes, and their nuclei contain prominent nucleoli. In the medulla, the thymic corpuscles or Hassall corpuscles, which are large collections of thymic epithelial cells.
  • Thymic epithelial cells function to 1) form a blood-thymus barrier to shield developing thymocytes from exposure to antigens, 2) compartmentalize the thymus to sequester immature and mature thymocytes, in the cortex and medulla, respectively, 3) provide a structural and supportive framework for the developing thymocytes (the thymus lacks reticular fibers), and 4) present self and foreign antigens to developing thymocytes during positive and negative selection.

questions.stemHtml: Level of visceral pleura goes upto which of the following levels during deep inspiration:
questions.solutionHtml:
B
  • During deep inspiration the lower border of the lung reaches level B anteriorly.
  • The lower border of the lung extends till the 6th rib in the midclavicular line, 8th rib in mid axillary line and 10th rib in mid scapular line.
  • During quiet breathing, the diaphragm moves about 1.5 cm.
  • During deep breathing; however, it moves by 6-10 cm thus extending up to the level of the 6th rib or 11th thoracic vertebra on the right side.
  • On full expiration, it extends up to 4th costal cartilage anteriorly, posteriorly up to the 8th vertebra.
  • This corresponds to a line dividing the liver in upper 1/3rd and middle 1/3rd marked as B in the given Image.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-995,996, 996.e1.

questions.stemHtml: Muscle attached to marked area:
questions.solutionHtml:
Opponens pollicis
  • Origin: trapezium and transverse carpal ligament.
  • Insertion: Metacarpal bone of the thumb on its radial side.
  • Innervation: Recurrent branch of the median nerve, also ulnar nerve.
  • Actions: Flexion of the thumb's metacarpal at the first carpometacarpal joint, which aids in opposition of the thumb.
  • Arterial supply: Superficial palmar arch.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-975,976.
